issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as double, while the reference solution implements these attributes as int. This inconsistency can confuse students about which data type to use when adding attributes and implementing related methods.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute types consistent across materials. Preferably update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as int to match the solution and typical use, or alternatively change the solution and template to use double for these attributes and update related methods accordingly.

issues.description: Within the problem statement UML the student-count attributes are typed as double but getTotalNumberOfStudents() is specified to return int. This creates an internal contradiction in the specification about the expected return type for the total number of students.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the internal UML contradiction by making types consistent: either change the attribute types in the UML to int (so getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning int is consistent), or change getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return double if the attributes should remain double. Update the template and solution to match the chosen approach.
